title: LLMs Homogenize Values in Constructive Arguments on Value-Laden Topics
benchmark_measurement: The study measured how Large Language Models (LLMs) homogenize human values when rewriting comments on value-laden topics. Specifically for religion, it analyzed how an LLM reshaped values in comments written in response to Islamophobic online threads, and how participants' own religious identities (Christian, Muslim, Hindu, Atheist) influenced the values they expressed in their writing.
findings: When rewriting comments on Islamophobic threads, the LLM (GPT-4) systematically downplayed Conservative values like Security (e.g., concerns about terrorism) and Tradition, while amplifying prosocial values like Universalism (e.g., tolerance) and Benevolence. This process often altered the original stance of comments critical of Islam, making them appear more neutral or supportive. Muslim participants tended to express more Traditional values, highlighting peaceful teachings, while Christian participants emphasized Universalism. Consequently, participants who were critical of Islam found the original human-written comments more aligned with their values, whereas those supportive of Islam preferred the LLM-rewritten versions.
